test_title: SSC Selection Post HSC Level Official Paper (Held on: 16 March 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: By selling an article for ₹390, a shopkeeper suffers some loss. Had he sold it for ₹444, he would have earned a profit equal to one-fifth of the loss he had in the earlier case. If he sells it for ₹522, what will be his profit percentage?
solution:
**Formula:**

P = SP - CP

P% = Pover CP × 100, where

P = Profit

P% = Profit percentage

CP = Cost Price

SP = Selling Price

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the article be "a".

According to the question-

⇒ 444 - a = 1over5 ×( a - 390)

⇒ 2220 - 5a = a - 390

⇒ 2220 + 390 = a + 5a

⇒ a = 2610over6 = Rs 435

Profit = Rs 522 - Rs 435 = Rs 87

Profit % = 87over435 × 100 = 20%

∴** The profit percentage on the transaction is 20%.**
